pages.summary: An object that checks a function's inputs and gives their values by name.
body: A function makes an `inputParser`, says what inputs it takes, and parses `varargin`: `addRequired` for inputs that must come first, `addOptional` for positional ones with defaults, `addParameter` for name-value pairs with defaults (`addParamValue` is the older name). Each may have a validation function, true for a good value (or an error for a bad one). After `parse`, `p.Results` holds every value by name and `p.UsingDefaults` lists those not given. `KeepUnmatched`, `CaseSensitive` and `PartialMatching` (on: `'Col'` matches `'Color'`) set how names are matched.

examples.title: A function with a required, an optional and a named input
examples.output:
ans =

    'Hello, Ada. '

ans =

    'Hello, Ada! Hello, Ada! '

The value of 'times' is invalid. It must satisfy the function: @(x)isnumeric(x)&&x>=1.

pages.summary: The message for a number of inputs outside a range: the older form of narginchk.
body: Empty when `n` is within `[low, high]`, else the message (or a struct with the message and identifier), for a function to pass to `error`.

examples.title: Within the range, and not
examples.output:
ans =

  logical

   1

ans =

    'Too many input arguments.'

pages.summary: Validation functions for signs: an error unless every element is positive, nonnegative, negative, nonpositive, or nonzero.
body: They give nothing when the value is fine and an error saying what was wanted when it is not; written in an `arguments` block after an input, or called directly. NaN fails all of them.

examples.title: Checked in a function's arguments block
examples.output:
ans =

     6

Invalid argument at position 2. Value must be positive.

examples.title: Called directly
examples.code:
mustBeNonnegative([0 1 2])
try, mustBeNonzero([1 0 2]), catch e, disp(e.message), end

pages.summary: Validation functions for kinds of numbers: whole, numeric, numeric or logical, floating point, real, finite, not NaN, not missing.
body: `mustBeInteger` is about the values (whole numbers, of any numeric class); `mustBeNumeric` and `mustBeFloat` about the class; `mustBeNonmissing` also rejects missing strings.

examples.title: Values that pass and one that fails each
examples.code:
mustBeInteger([1 2 3])
try, mustBeInteger(2.5), catch e, disp(e.message), end
try, mustBeFinite([1 Inf]), catch e, disp(e.message), end
try, mustBeNumeric('7'), catch e, disp(e.message), end
examples.output:
Value must be integer.
Value must be finite.
Value must be numeric.

pages.summary: Validation functions by comparison: above or below a number, within bounds, or one of a set.
body: `mustBeInRange(A, lower, upper)` includes the bounds unless `'exclusive'`, `'exclude-lower'` or `'exclude-upper'` says otherwise; `mustBeMember(A, S)` takes numbers or texts.

examples.title: Bounds and a set
examples.code:
mustBeInRange([0 0.5 1], 0, 1)
try, mustBeInRange(1, 0, 1, 'exclusive'), catch e, disp(e.message), end
mustBeMember('red', {'red', 'green'})
try, mustBeMember(4, [1 2 3]), catch e, disp(e.message), end
examples.output:
Value must be greater than 0 and less than 1.
Value must be a member of this set:
    1
    2
    3

pages.summary: Validation functions for shape: not empty, not sparse, a row or column, at most one element.

examples.title: A row passes, a matrix does not
examples.code:
mustBeVector([1 2 3])
try, mustBeVector(magic(3)), catch e, disp(e.message), end
try, mustBeScalarOrEmpty([1 2]), catch e, disp(e.message), end
examples.output:
Value must be a 1-by-n or n-by-1 vector.
Value must be scalar or empty.

pages.summary: Validation functions for text: any text, a single text, text with characters in every element, and a valid variable name.
body: Text is a character vector, a string array or (for `mustBeText`) a cell array of character vectors.
syntax: One text: a character vector or a string scalar.

examples.title: Texts checked
examples.code:
mustBeText({'a', 'b'})
try, mustBeTextScalar(["a" "b"]), catch e, disp(e.message), end
try, mustBeValidVariableName('2fast'), catch e, disp(e.message), end
examples.output:
Value must be a character vector or a string scalar.
Value must be a valid variable name.

pages.summary: Validation functions for class: one of the classes named.
body: `mustBeA` takes class names, and `'numeric'`, `'float'` and `'integer'` for groups of classes; a class derived from one named passes. `mustBeUnderlyingType` checks the class itself.

examples.title: Classes and groups
examples.code:
mustBeA(int8(3), 'integer')
mustBeA('text', {'char', 'string'})
try, mustBeA(3, 'integer'), catch e, disp(e.message), end
examples.output: Value must be one of the following types: 'integer'.

pages.summary: Validation functions for paths: each name an existing file, or an existing folder.

examples.title: A file made, and one that is not there
examples.code:
fid = fopen('notes.txt', 'w'); fclose(fid);
mustBeFile('notes.txt')
mustBeFolder('.')
try, mustBeFile('missing.txt'), catch e, disp(e.message), end
examples.output: The following files do not exist: 'missing.txt'.
